subject: Materials Science
title: Fullerenes: The Carbon Cage
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Fullerenes: The Carbon Cage.

hook.text: C₆₀ — sixty carbon atoms in a perfect soccer ball shape — discovered in 1985 and named after Buckminster Fuller.

buildup.text: Buckminsterfullerene has 20 hexagons and 12 pentagons — the same geometry as a truncated icosahedron.

discovery.text: Fullerenes can trap atoms inside their cage — endohedral fullerenes encapsulate metals for medical imaging contrast.

twist.text: C₆₀ was expected to revolutionize materials — but nanotubes and graphene stole the spotlight within a decade.

climax.text: Fullerene derivatives are used in organic solar cells — accepting electrons efficiently in polymer blends.

punchline.text: Sixty carbon atoms in a cage — geometry that launched the nanotech era.

quiz.question: What is a unique capability of fullerenes?
options: They can trap atoms inside their hollow cage structure
They are the strongest carbon allotrope
They conduct electricity better than copper
